corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN. The step is a textbook rescaling of a positively homogeneous objective. The s=1 case (Gamma_1 = p/(p-1)) is prior art: it is written out in Kam et al. 2026, App. A.3.2, Eq. (18), and it is classical in graph-spectral form (Fiedler 1973, §3.5-3.6). The rescaling itself is the one in Sun-Boyd-Xiao-Diaconis 2006 (FMMP, §2 and §3.2). The l_{1/s} version for s>1 was not found; its novelty is the novelty of the programme (R4). Present prop:coverage as a normalisation, not a contribution.
issues:
1) The checker misdescribes Kam et al. (arXiv 2609.17926). I re-fetched it: 15 Sep 2026, under review at NeurReps 2026, and the bib entry is correct. The checker says the "return x budget" rescaling is "implicit, with exponent 2". In fact the proof of Prop. 5, Eq. (18), states "Delta_S(beta) <= (p/(p-1)) sum_k beta_k <= (p/(p-1)) sqrt(K_max) ||beta||_2", using sum_{s!=0}(1-cos) = p. The first inequality is prop:coverage at s=1 with Gamma_1 = p/(p-1). It is also, step for step, the averaging proof in app:dense (appendix.tex line 28). The l2 budget enters only through the Cauchy-Schwarz step. The difference from the paper is that Kam applies it to idealised amplitude-only logits, not to arbitrary networks. Kam is contemporaneous (10 days before the deadline).

2) The checker missed classical graph-spectral prior art. F_y(delta) = sum_j y_j kappa_j(delta) is the delta-th Laplacian eigenvalue of the weighted circulant Cay(Z_p, +-j), so Gamma_s is the largest spectral gap under an l_{1/s} weight budget.
(a) Fiedler 1973, Czech. Math. J. 23:298-305, §3.5 Lemma: "lambda_2 <= [n/(n-1)] min m_ii" for PSD M with Me=0. §3.6: a(K_n)=n. Together these give Gamma_1 <= p/(p-1) sum y_j, with equality for uniform weights. That is exactly the s=1 coverage bound and the inequality in cor:dense. The uniqueness part of cor:dense is not in Fiedler.
(b) Sun, Boyd, Xiao, Diaconis, SIAM Review 48(4):681-699 (2006), the FMMP paper. Problem (1) maximises lambda_2(w) subject to a linear budget. They note "Since lambda_2 is a positive homogeneous function of w ... the inequality constraint always holds with equality", and §3.2 eq. (2) rescales to "minimize cost s.t. lambda_2 >= 1". This is the same move as prop:coverage and the appendix reduction Gamma_s = (min phi)^{-s}. Gamma_1 is FMMP on K_p restricted to circulant rates. The concave-budget case s>1 is not FMMP: it is non-convex, and no source was found for it.

3) Morwani (arXiv 2311.07568; Spotlight at ICLR 2024; confirmed). The more precise pointer for the s=1 budget linearity is Lemma 5, "Combining neurons": "If b = nu ... for any neuron scaling factors sum lambda_i^nu = 1 ...". Section 4 alone is less precise.

4) Search caveats. WebSearch was exhausted (200/200) and the S2 and arXiv APIs returned 429. I searched OpenAlex (10 queries) and MathOverflow/Math.SE through the StackExchange API (8 queries). They turned up only adjacent Chowla-type hits (MO 209071 and 209236), which maximise a trough rather than minimise a sidelobe, so they don't apply. No l_q (q<1) budget version of lambda_2 or cosine-coverage maximisation was found.

Recommended fix: after prop:coverage, add one sentence identifying Gamma_s as the l_{1/s}-budget spectral gap of a weighted circulant, crediting sun2006fastest for the s=1 problem and the rescaling, and kam2026symmetry Eq. (18) for the concurrent s=1 bound. At cor:dense, cite fiedler1973algebraic §3.5-3.6 for the inequality. extra_citations.why: The §3.5 Lemma (lambda_2 <= n/(n-1) min_i m_ii for PSD M with Me=0) and §3.6 (a(K_n)=n) give the s=1 coverage bound Gamma_1 <= p/(p-1) sum_j y_j, with equality for uniform weights. That is the inequality in cor:dense and prop:coverage at s=1. Classical; cite at cor:dense/app:dense. PDF read in full on dml.cz.

Problem (1) maximises lambda_2(w) subject to a linear budget on the weights, using the positive homogeneity of lambda_2 and the rescaling in §3.2. Gamma_1(p) is this problem on K_p restricted to circulant rates, and prop:coverage and the appendix reduction are the same rescaling. Gamma_s for s>1 is the concave-budget generalisation, which I did not find in the literature. Cite at prop:coverage or eq:programme.
